findings.description: The ledger_exports bucket stores financial ledger exports but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects are not encrypted under an operator-controlled key. Data at rest is left to provider defaults rather than an explicit SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 policy.
The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving report data unencrypted at rest under any explicitly managed key.
The model_artifacts bucket defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model artifacts are stored without explicitly configured encryption at rest.
The ops_runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, storing operational runbooks without explicitly configured encryption at rest.

This object uploads vendor-roster.xlsx into reports_archive, which has no default encryption configured, and the object itself sets no server_side_encryption; a vendor roster likely containing third-party/PII data is therefore stored without encryption at rest.

The audit_trail bucket sets acl = "lcatalogopts-delivery-write", which is not a valid S3 canned ACL and is not "private". Applying a non-default, unrecognized ACL to the bucket holding audit logs risks an unintended/unpredictable access grant on security-relevant data.
